summary: This bill requires federal agencies to charge labor organizations fees for the use of agency resources and employee time, with penalties for non-payment including denial of union time, cessation of agency resource use, and eventual termination of the labor organization's certification as an exclusive representative.

scores.thoughts: This bill aims to reduce government spending by requiring federal labor organizations to pay for the agency resources and employee time they use, which is currently borne by the taxpayer. By shifting these costs, the bill directly seeks to decrease expenditures from the general fund of the Treasury.

The bill requires federal agencies to charge recognized labor unions quarterly fees equal to the value of official union time and agency resources used, with all payments transferred directly to the Treasury general fund. This cost-recovery mechanism is the sole purpose of the legislation and is explicitly framed as protecting taxpayers, making revenue generation and deficit reduction central to the bill as a whole.
